audit.why: Level 1 skill, Gangplank taking levels 2-3 and everything from first item on, with the Levels 4-5 / Level 6 transform window even, matches a 53.33% Gangplank win rate: Gnar's power is a rage-gated burst window, Gangplank's is compounding item scaling.
audit.corrected: Chart left as-is; the full and content layers already agree row for row.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Mega transform spike gave no cooldown for GNAR! and offered no positional answer to the wall stun.
audit.why: GNAR! is 90/60/30 — by rank 2 it is back every 60s, so 'wait it out' is not the plan; standing away from walls is, because the stun and bonus damage only trigger on a wall hit.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text now names Rage Gene, gives the 60s rank-2 cooldown, and tells you to fight in open ground with no wall behind you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hyper is called a passive that procs 'every 3rd hit' for 'bonus damage + slow'. Hyper is Gnar's W in mini form, and Riot's text gives bonus damage and MOVE SPEED — no slow. Gnar's actual passive is Rage Gene. Mega Gnar's W, Wallop, is a stun and was never mentioned even though it is the CC you will actually eat in a Mega trade.
audit.why: Riot W text: 'Gnar's attacks and spells hype him up, dealing bonus damage and granting him Move Speed. Mega Gnar ... can rear up on his hind legs and smash down on the area in front of him, stunning enemies in an area.' Passive is Rage Gene. A slow that does not exist changes how you decide to disengage — that is the kind of error that gets a player killed.
audit.corrected: Hyper corrected to (W), bonus damage and move speed, in whys[0], spikes[0] and early. Wallop (W) named as Mega's 7s stun in mid, alongside the GNAR! wall stun, with Remove Scurvy's 18s at rank 3 as the single cleanse you have to spend on one of them.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Out-ranges your Parrrley" was stated without numbers.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw is 1100 to Parrrley's 625 — a 475-unit gap that explains why you cannot answer the poke at all, and why the keg is the only tool that reaches him.
audit.corrected: Both ranges stated in whys[0], spikes[0] and early; the boomerang-catch cooldown reduction off a 16s base added to early.

audit.why: The packet flags 'Powder Kegs' as a probable wrong name at distance 1. It is a false positive — it is the correct name pluralised. My rewrite of 'early' happens to make it singular anyway.
audit.corrected: No name change made on that basis.

edits.before: Mini-Gnar's Boomerang Throw (Q) out-ranges your Parrrley and his Hyper passive (bonus damage + slow on every 3rd hit) punishes you if you walk up — the early short trades go to him.
edits.after: Mini-Gnar's Boomerang Throw (Q) reaches 1100 to your Parrrley's 625, and Hyper (W) gives him bonus damage and move speed if you walk up — the early short trades go to him.

edits.before: Mini-Gnar out-ranges you: Boomerang Throw (Q) pokes from outside Parrrley range and his Hyper passive (every 3rd hit on the same target = bonus damage + slow) chunks you if you walk up to last-hit. Eat the poke and farm safe — your kegs aren't online to fight back yet.
edits.after: Mini-Gnar out-ranges you: Boomerang Throw (Q) pokes at 1100 from outside your 625 Parrrley, and Hyper (W) gives him bonus damage and move speed to chase you off a last-hit. Eat the poke and farm safe — your kegs aren't online to fight back yet.

edits.before: Gnar's biggest swing: a full Rage Bar turns him into mega-Gnar with GNAR! (R), which throws you and stuns if you hit a wall — plus a big tankiness spike. If he catches your all-in here he flips the trade, so don't commit while the bar is near full.
edits.after: Gnar's biggest swing: a full Rage Gene bar turns him Mega, and GNAR! (R) throws you — a stun if you hit a wall, and it is only 60s at rank 2. Fight in open ground with no wall behind you, and never commit while the bar is near full.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to mini-Gnar. Boomerang Throw (Q) out-ranges your Parrrley, and if you walk up to last-hit he stacks his Hyper passive — every third hit on you deals bonus damage and slows, so the short trades go his way. Don't try to fight here: your Powder Kegs have long cooldowns and aren't online to punish him yet. Last-hit at max Parrrley range, accept some boomerang poke, and watch his Rage Bar — you do NOT want to be caught in an all-in when it fills into mega.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to mini-Gnar. Boomerang Throw (Q) reaches 1100 against your 625 Parrrley, and Hyper (W) hypes his attacks for bonus damage and move speed, so he wins every short trade you walk up for — and if he catches the returning boomerang its 16s cooldown drops. Don't fight here: your Powder Keg has a long cooldown and isn't online to punish him. Last-hit at max Parrrley range, accept the poke, and watch Rage Gene — never be mid-commit when the bar fills into Mega.

edits.before: At 4-5 you stabilize. A second Parrrley and Powder Keg point let you place a barrel and Q-detonate it from range, chunking mini-Gnar without stepping into his boomerang. The one danger is the transform: when the Rage Bar fills, GNAR! (R) throws you and stuns if you hit a wall, and mega-Gnar gets a real tankiness spike — so save W (Remove Scurvy) to cleanse that stun and heal the poke rather than burning it early. Bait the mega timer: trade hard while he's fragile mini, back off the instant the bar caps.
edits.after: At 4-5 you stabilize. A second Parrrley and keg point let you place a barrel and Q-detonate from range, chunking mini-Gnar without stepping into his boomerang. The danger is the transform: Mega trades Hyper for Wallop (W), a 7s stun, and GNAR! (R) throws you for a second stun into a wall. Hold Remove Scurvy for whichever lands rather than burning it on chip — it is down 18s at rank 3. Trade hard while he is fragile mini, and back off the instant the bar caps.

notes: The 'Hyper passive ... bonus damage + slow' claim was wrong twice over: Hyper is the mini-form W, not the passive (Rage Gene is), and it grants Gnar move speed rather than slowing you. Fixed in the three places it appeared. wants.you[0] still says 'eating Hyper procs' — that phrasing survives the correction, so I left it. Remove Scurvy cleansing the GNAR! wall stun is inherited text I kept: Riot's W text says it cures crowd control effects and a stun is CC, but whether the airborne portion of the throw is cleansed is not answerable from the kit file, so I did not extend the claim to the displacement.
